correctness.rationale: All-seat-two JR is exactly the 2*u<n condition. By maximum candidate support, either every pair is JR, or every JR pair can reach a common candidate in one valid swap; the tied-support case uses a complementary-support witness and contradiction. The common-pivot clique gives three swaps. The 5-candidate 6-voter instance has JR endpoints but no JR cross pair, proving distance three. Finite enumeration of every anonymous approval profile for five candidates and at most five voters proves the sharp electorate cutoff and is independently replayable from verify.cpp.

value.rationale: The 2025 foundational paper has exact-JR disconnectedness for k>=3 but only approximate-JR guaranteed paths generally. The unrestricted positive k=2 connectivity theorem with a constant exact-JR distance is a meaningful structural boundary; its sharp five-candidate/six-voter nongeodesic example explains why auxiliary candidates can be indispensable. The finite minimum fixes a natural first obstruction rather than an arbitrary table cell.
